text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: ap-east-1 control-plane heartbeats silent for 90s, health checks failing, 0/48 GPU hosts responding. severity=critical :rotating_light:

alisha: seeing the same on Grafana dash, pod status unknown for scheduler and controller-manager clusters in ap-east-1

kai: can folks confirm BGP/ASN level? last change was a provider patch 12:02 UTC

ben: i can ssh into one of the edge jump hosts but cannot reach kube-api on control plane IPs, tcp 6443 times out

maria: logs show control-plane leader election flapping, kubelet heartbeats not present. attaching last 3 lines: ```
I0318 12:11:22.345 kubelet: heartbeat missed for node gpu-12
I0318 12:11:22.347 controller: failed to contact etcd cluster: rpc timeout
I0318 12:11:22.351 scheduler: api-server unreachable (dial tcp 10.0.0.5:6443: i/o timeout)
```

oncall-sre: acknowledged, mobilizing incident. alisha and kai, please run quick reachability matrix and post results. priority: route traffic off ap-east-1 if we cannot restore in 10m

alisha: quick checks: control-plane AS numbers show routes withdrawn from provider A. traceroute to 10.0.0.5 drops at provider AS64512

kai: contacting provider on emergency channel now (ticket TS-AP-4012). they report intermittent fabric control-plane issue in ap-east PoP cluster. ETA unknown

ben: queuing failover plan — want to confirm capacity in ap-south-1 and us-west-2 for GPU-heavy traffic. current free GPU slots: ap-south-1: 120, us-west-2: 60 (from capacity dashboard)

maria: model-serving routes include dynamic fallback to region: [ap-south-1, us-west-2] per routing policy. however, latency for apac clients will increase ~120-200ms, and cost per token +25% on average

oncall-sre: start traffic-shift runbook step 1 — mark ap-east-1 as draining in routing control plane, enable basin fallback. alisha, apply routing patch (k8s-configmap -> rtpolicies/fallback)

alisha: applying patch now: ```kubectl patch configmap rtpolicies -n infra --patch '{"data":{"ap-east-1":"drain"}}'```

deploy-bot: configmap rtpolicies patched by alisha at 12:18 UTC

networking-lead: before full shift, advise throttle of batch jobs that would saturate new regions. setting queue-limit to 0.5x for long-running batches

kai: provider responded — they confirm control-plane fabric rebooting, nexus mgmt-plane flapping. they have engineers onsite, no ETA yet. recommended we keep failover in place

oncall-sre: rolling traffic shift to next region. executing step: update edge routing and CDN fallback. @ben can you validate service endpoints post-shift?

ben: running synthetic probes to frontend edge -> backend in ap-south-1 and us-west-2. ap-south-1 OK for small bursts, us-west-2 saturated at 80% but still serving. probes: ```200 OK /health 3/3; p50 latency ap-south-1 48ms; us-west-2 220ms; errors none```

maria: increment alert paging to incident channel and notify support/CS about degraded APAC experience for next 2-4 hours. prepping status message draft

oncall-sre: decision: keep ap-east-1 drained, continue failover. escalate to infra leadership for capacity commit if this hits >4h. actions: (1) maintain traffic shift, (2) throttle non-essential jobs, (3) open capacity order with cloud-sales, (4) monitor provider updates. owners: alisha, ben, kai

alisha: noted. collecting final screenshots and will kick off postmortem template when region recovers

networking-lead: also toggled BGP graceful reset settings to avoid flap storms during provider reconvergence

monitoring-bot: NOTE: automated remediation attempted (restart control-plane services) at 12:16 UTC — failed due to rpc timeouts. next automated retry disabled per incident runbook

oncall-sre: thanks team. keeping channel open for updates. if provider gives ETA update, paste here. moving to incident bridge in 5m :phone
